summary: Introduces WiserUI-Bench, pairing real UI variants from industry A/B tests with observed behavioral winners and expert explanations. It evaluates models’ ability to predict the more effective interface and explain its effect on user behavior.

name: Seed1.5-VL Technical Report
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GUI control is one agent task within a broader vision-language model report.
summary: Reports Seed1.5-VL, a general vision-language model evaluated on GUI control and gameplay alongside visual understanding and reasoning tasks.

name: Grounded Reinforcement Learning for Visual Reasoning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). GUI localization is one part of a broader visual reasoning evaluation.
summary: Introduces ViGoRL, a visual reasoning model trained to reference image coordinates and zoom during reasoning; its evaluations include GUI element localization.

name: Open CaptchaWorld: A Comprehensive Web-based Platform for Testing and Benchmarking Multimodal LLM Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.
summary: Open CaptchaWorld evaluates multimodal agents on interactive browser-based CAPTCHA puzzles. Its benchmark distinguishes task success from the depth of visual reasoning and interaction needed to complete a puzzle.

name: FormFactory: An Interactive Benchmarking Suite for Multimodal Form-Filling Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces FormFactory, an interactive web-based benchmark for agents filling online forms, with varied field formats and evaluation of instruction-to-field alignment.

name: FormGym: Doing Paperwork with Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v4).
summary: Introduces FormGym, a benchmark for filling image-only forms, and FieldFinder, a tool that helps LLMs locate where to place text on those forms.

name: DiMo-GUI: Advancing Test-time Scaling in GUI Grounding via Modality-Aware Visual Reasoning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Separates textual and iconic UI elements and iteratively focuses visual regions to refine grounding without additional model training.

name: R-VLM: Region-Aware Vision Language Model for Precise GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: R-VLM localizes GUI elements through zoomed-in region proposals and an intersection-over-union-aware training objective. It evaluates the grounding model on ScreenSpot and AgentStudio and studies its effect on navigation in AITW and Mind2Web.

name: A Training-Free, Task-Agnostic Framework for Enhancing MLLM Performance on High-Resolution Images
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The method is task-agnostic and is also evaluated on 4K and 8K image perception.
summary: Introduces Extract Candidate then Predict (ECP), a training-free two-stage method for high-resolution images, evaluated partly on 4K GUI grounding.

name: Screen2AX: Vision-Based Approach for Automatic macOS Accessibility Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Screen2AX, which creates hierarchical accessibility metadata from macOS screenshots, plus datasets and Screen2AX-Task for desktop-agent evaluation.

name: Phi-Ground Tech Report: Advancing Perception in GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Reports a GUI-grounding model family and empirical design choices covering source data, perception training, and coordinate prediction.

name: Uncertainty-Aware GUI Agent: Adaptive Perception through Component Recommendation and Human-in-the-Loop Refinement
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: RecAgent narrows attention to recommended UI components and requests user feedback when task intent or decisions remain uncertain. It introduces ComplexAction to evaluate specified single-step GUI actions in difficult interface scenarios.

name: Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: D2Snap reduces serialized DOM observations while preserving actionable elements and features that distinguish their uses. The study compares reduced DOM inputs with screenshot-based observations for a web agent on tasks sampled from Online-Mind2Web.

name: FineState-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Fine-Grained State Control in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: FineState-Bench evaluates fine-grained GUI perception and control across desktop, web, and mobile interfaces. Its Visual Diagnostic Assistant separates perception and localization contributions in controlled interaction experiments.

name: V2P: Visual Attention Calibration for GUI Grounding via Background Suppression and Center Peaking
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: V2P trains GUI grounding by suppressing attention to background regions and emphasizing the center of the target element. It represents target importance with size-dependent Gaussian heatmaps and evaluates the contribution of each component on ScreenSpot-v2 and ScreenSpot-Pro.

name: Structuring GUI Elements through Vision Language Models: Towards Action Space Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces IAML training, which augments coordinate samples to help multimodal models locate GUI elements from screen content and user instructions.

name: WebMMU: A Benchmark for Multimodal Multilingual Website Understanding and Code Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces WebMMU, a multilingual benchmark for website visual question answering, element grounding, code editing, and mockup-to-code generation.

publication.title: DashboardQA: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Question Answering on Interactive Dashboards
publication.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EACL 2026

name: DashboardQA: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Question Answering on Interactive Dashboards
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The benchmark centers on interactive dashboards from Tableau Public.
summary: Introduces DashboardQA to evaluate how vision-language GUI agents answer questions by interacting with dashboards, grounding elements, and planning actions.

name: PG-Agent: An Agent Powered by Page Graph
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces PG-Agent, which turns GUI operation episodes into page graphs and retrieves guidance from them to support task decomposition in new scenarios.

name: Learning Active Perception via Self-Evolving Preference Optimization for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: LASER builds preference data for multi-step GUI perception by combining Monte Carlo quality estimates with region-overlap evaluation. Its self-evolving training encourages relevant region selection and adapts the amount of reasoning before predicting screen coordinates.

name: SparkUI-Parser: Enhancing GUI Perception with Robust Grounding and Parsing
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.
summary: Introduces SparkUI-Parser, which adds continuous coordinate decoding and a rejection mechanism for nonexistent targets to a multimodal model. It also presents ScreenParse for evaluating structural interface perception.

name: How Auxiliary Reasoning Unleashes GUI Grounding in VLMs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies the gap between latent visual grounding and explicit coordinate output in general vision-language models. Three zero-shot methods add axes, grids, or labeled intersections to GUI screenshots so models can express spatial locations without fine-tuning.

name: GUI-ARP: Enhancing Grounding with Adaptive Region Perception for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-ARP uses visual attention to crop relevant screenshot regions and decides whether a target needs single-stage or multi-stage analysis. Supervised fine-tuning followed by GRPO trains this adaptive procedure for high-resolution GUI grounding.

name: Benchmarking MLLM-based Web Understanding: Reasoning, Robustness and Safety
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates multimodal LLMs on web interface reasoning, visual perturbation robustness, and safety-critical web understanding tasks.

name: GUI-PRA: Process Reward Agent for GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: GUI-PRA evaluates GUI progress by generating task-specific criteria and actively inspecting visual evidence with tools. It tests offline judgment on OS-Critic Bench and the effects of this feedback on online mobile policies in AndroidWorld.

name: GUI-KV: Efficient GUI Agents via KV Cache with Spatio-Temporal Awareness
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: GUI-KV compresses vision-language agents’ attention caches using visual-token saliency and redundancy between screenshot frames. The method requires no retraining and evaluates how cache budgets affect GUI action accuracy and computational cost.

name: FocusAgent: Simple Yet Effective Ways of Trimming the Large Context of Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Results are reported on WorkArena and WebArena; the injection result concerns a FocusAgent variant.
summary: Introduces FocusAgent, which uses a lightweight LLM to select task-relevant lines from web agents' accessibility-tree observations, reducing context size and exposure to prompt injection.

name: Improving GUI Grounding with Explicit Position-to-Coordinate Mapping
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: This work addresses GUI localization errors caused by mismatches between visual patch positions and output pixel coordinates. RULER tokens provide explicit coordinate references, while Interleaved MRoPE balances width and height encoding; evaluation uses the ScreenSpot benchmark family.

name: State Your Intention to Steer Your Attention: An AI Assistant for Intentional Digital Living
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces an assistant that reads screenshots, application titles, and URLs to compare computer activity with a user's stated intention and send notifications when it diverges.

name: GUIrilla: A Scalable Framework for Automated Desktop UI Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUIrilla systematically explores macOS interfaces to collect interaction traces and accessibility metadata for downstream GUI research. It organizes these observations into hierarchical MacApp Trees and describes an accessibility-driven collection library.

name: GUI Knowledge Bench: Revealing the Knowledge Gap of VLMs in GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: GUI Knowledge Bench tests knowledge of widgets, interactions, and procedures across six named platforms and 292 applications to assess VLMs used for GUI tasks.

name: GUI-AIMA: Aligning Intrinsic Multimodal Attention with a Context Anchor for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces GUI-AIMA, which supervises instruction-relevant attention over visual patches. Patch-level grounding can be combined with an optional zoom stage and is evaluated across GUI localization benchmarks.

name: MEGA-GUI: Multi-stage Enhanced Grounding Agents for GUI Elements
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces MEGA-GUI, which separates coarse region selection from fine-grained interface-element grounding. Bidirectional zooming and context-aware instruction rewriting coordinate specialized vision-language agents across visual scales.

name: Prune4Web: DOM Tree Pruning Programming for Web Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Prune4Web, where generated scoring programs filter DOM elements according to decomposed subtasks before grounding. An annotation pipeline and two-turn training procedure coordinate the planner, programmatic filter and grounder.

name: Qwen3-VL Technical Report
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract, which positions the models for agentic decision-making but names no GUI environment; the GUI-operation claim comes from the curated Qwen3-VL repository README.
summary: Describes the Qwen3-VL dense and MoE vision-language models, with 256K-token interleaved context, interleaved-MRoPE, DeepStack and textual video timestamps; a general foundation model aimed partly at agentic use.

name: MPR-GUI: Benchmarking and Enhancing Multilingual Perception and Reasoning in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: MPR-GUI evaluates GUI perception and reasoning through strictly aligned tasks in six languages. GUI-XLI adjusts non-English hidden representations toward English representations at language-sensitive layers during inference to address the measured cross-language gaps.

name: Zoom in, Click out: Unlocking and Evaluating the Potential of Zooming for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: ZoomClick uses repeated zooming and context adjustment to improve GUI grounding without training. The paper studies zoom depth, crop sizes, and related choices and introduces GUIZoom-Bench to evaluate how grounding models respond to zoomed views.

name: DAVE: A VLM Vision Encoder for Document Understanding and Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: DAVE trains a vision encoder for document images and web agents using self-supervised pretraining followed by supervised parsing and localization. It combines decoder-specific encoder merging with feature fusion and evaluates web localization and agent benchmarks alongside document tasks.

name: iSHIFT: Lightweight Slow-Fast GUI Agent with Adaptive Perception
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces iSHIFT, which combines latent reasoning with perception-control tokens to adapt GUI inference. The agent switches between detailed regional grounding and faster use of global visual cues.

name: FocusUI: Efficient UI Grounding via Position-Preserving Visual Token Selection
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: FocusUI selects instruction-relevant screenshot patches while preserving their positional structure for GUI grounding. Its PosPad scheme replaces runs of dropped tokens with positional markers and is evaluated under reduced token budgets.

name: GUI-Eyes: Tool-Augmented Perception for Visual Grounding in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: GUI-Eyes trains GUI grounders to decide when and how to use visual tools such as crops and zooms. Its coarse-to-fine policy uses dense spatial rewards based on location proximity and region overlap, with evaluation on ScreenSpot-Pro.

name: Generative Visual Code Mobile World Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: gWorld predicts future mobile GUI states as renderable web code and supplies an automated pipeline for code-based training data. The study evaluates visual state prediction and how stronger world models affect downstream mobile policies.

name: Trifuse: Enhancing Attention-Based GUI Grounding via Multimodal Fusion
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Trifuse combines attention-based localization with OCR text cues and icon captions to ground GUI instructions. Its fusion procedure favors cross-modal agreement and sharp location peaks, and is evaluated without task-specific fine-tuning.

name: Where Not to Learn: Prior-Aligned Training with Subset-based Attribution Constraints
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v6). GUI-agent click decisions are one of two evaluation settings; the other is image classification.
summary: Proposes training with subset-based attribution constraints so models attend to intended evidence, evaluated on image classification and GUI-agent click decisions.

name: GUI-GenBench: Evaluating Image Generation Models as Interactive GUI Environments
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: GUI-GenBench tests image-generation models as action-conditioned GUI environments across five suites, including transitions, trajectories and grounding. Its VLM-based GUI-Score separates goal completion, interaction logic, consistency and visual properties.

name: Anonymization-Enhanced Privacy Protection for Mobile GUI Agents: Available but Invisible
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: An anonymization framework replaces sensitive screen content and instructions with consistent, type-preserving placeholders while mediating actions through a local interaction proxy. Experiments on AndroidLab and PrivScreen examine the privacy–utility trade-off when mobile GUI agents operate over these transformed interfaces.

name: ScreenParse: Moving Beyond Sparse Grounding with Complete Screen Parsing Supervision
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ScreenParse supplies dense annotations of UI elements, types and text in web screenshots through an automated rendering and filtering pipeline. ScreenVLM learns to output structured screen markup, and the study evaluates dense parsing and transfer to GUI grounding.

name: CoME: Empowering Channel-of-Mobile-Experts with Informative Hybrid-Capabilities Reasoning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces Channel-of-Mobile-Experts (CoME), a mobile agent with experts for screen summary, subtask planning, action decisions and action functions, trained in stages with InfoGain-Driven DPO (Info-DPO).

name: ST-Lite: Training-Free KV Cache Compression with Spatio-Trajectory Guidance for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces ST-Lite, a training-free KV cache compression scheme for vision-language GUI agents that filters redundant frames and preserves small UI elements in interaction traces.

name: PIRA-Bench: A Transition from Reactive GUI Agents to GUI-based Proactive Intent Recommendation Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: PIRA-Bench evaluates proactive intent recommendations from noisy GUI screenshot sequences containing interleaved tasks and user context. Its PIRF baseline combines memory and state tracking to maintain multiple task threads and identify opportunities to assist.

name: Zoom to Essence: Trainless GUI Grounding by Inferring upon Interface Elements
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents ZoomUI, a training-free grounding method that expresses instructions as visual element descriptions and uses model attention to zoom progressively into relevant interface regions. Evaluation examines instruction-to-element localization on GUI benchmarks.

name: GUI-CEval: A Hierarchical and Comprehensive Chinese Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-CEval evaluates Chinese mobile GUI agents through a hierarchy of atomic abilities and application-level tasks collected on physical devices. Its diagnostics cover perception, planning, reflection, execution and post-action evaluation across a broad set of apps.

name: WebPII: Benchmarking Visual PII Detection for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebPII provides synthetic e-commerce screenshots with fine-grained annotations for sensitive information, including partially filled forms and transaction identifiers. It also trains WebRedact to detect visual PII as a privacy component for computer-use agents.

name: AdaZoom-GUI: Adaptive Zoom-based GUI Grounding with Instruction Refinement
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Combines instruction rewriting with conditional second-stage zooming for small GUI targets. A grounding dataset and GRPO training support joint prediction of click coordinates and element bounding boxes.

name: MANA: Towards Efficient Mobile Ad Detection via Multimodal Agentic UI Navigation
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.
summary: MANA combines visual, temporal and exploration signals to guide navigation toward mobile advertisements. It evaluates ad detection and interaction cost on commercial smartphones, including obfuscated-ad cases.

name: GUIDE: A Benchmark for Understanding and Assisting Users in Open-Ended GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUIDE evaluates whether models can recognize a user’s behavior, infer intent and decide when to offer help during open-ended software tasks. It uses narrated screen recordings of novice users and studies the effect of additional user context on these assistance decisions.

name: Where and How to Prune: An Empirical Study of Visual Token Pruning for GUI Agent Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies visual token pruning for GUI navigation, separating reusable screenshot encoder embeddings from later language-model computation. The analysis examines foreground-background token allocation and spatial coverage when pruning historical screenshots.

name: MolmoPoint: Better Pointing for VLMs with Grounding Tokens
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent general VLM pointing method with an explicit GUI-grounding experiment; no autonomous GUI-task execution is established.
summary: MolmoPoint replaces textual coordinate generation with pointing tokens that select visual regions and refine them through subpatches. The general image/video method includes GUI-pointing evaluation on ScreenSpotPro alongside other visual grounding tasks.

name: PixelPrune: Pixel-Level Adaptive Visual Token Reduction via Predictive Coding
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent cross-domain VLM compression method with GUI-benchmark evaluation.
summary: PixelPrune removes pixel-redundant patches before the vision encoder, reducing both encoding and downstream language-model work. The training-free method evaluates lossless and controlled-lossy compression on document and GUI tasks.

name: Read More, Think More: Revisiting Observation Reduction for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Studies HTML and accessibility-tree observations for web agents, relating their usefulness to model capability and thinking budget, and proposes diff-based observation history to save tokens.

name: What's Missing in Screen-to-Action? Towards a UI-in-the-Loop Paradigm for Multimodal GUI Reasoning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces UILoop, which inserts explicit UI-element localization, function and usage reasoning between screen observation and action. UI Comprehension-Bench evaluates these element-level capabilities with three metrics.

name: Preference Redirection via Attention Concentration: An Attack on Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Creating the attack requires white-box access to the model.
summary: Introduces PRAC, an adversarial-patch attack that redirects a computer-use agent's visual attention to steer product selection on an online shopping platform.

name: PrecisionCUA: Iterative Visual Refinement for Pixel-Precise Cursor Grounding in Code Editors
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies iterative cursor grounding in dense code-editor interfaces, using visual feedback from earlier attempts to correct displacement. PrecisionCUA evaluates this closed-loop process across multiple model families on coding-interface tasks.

name: Do LLMs Need to See Everything? A Benchmark and Study of Failures in LLM-driven Smartphone Automation using Screentext vs. Screenshots
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: DailyDroid compares text-only and text-plus-screenshot agents on everyday Android tasks across multiple apps and difficulty levels. Its failure analysis examines accessibility, observation modality and agent/application behavior.

name: PageGuide: Browser extension to assist users in navigating a webpage and locating information
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v5). PageGuide assists users with navigation and verification; the abstract reports a user study.
summary: PageGuide is a browser extension that highlights evidence for answers on a page and guides users through web pages with evidence captured at each step.

name: AutoGUI-v2: A Comprehensive Multi-Modal GUI Functionality Understanding Benchmark
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: AutoGUI-v2 evaluates interface functionality, grounding and predicted interaction outcomes using hierarchical regions derived through VLM-human annotation. Its tasks span multiple operating systems and expose differences between functional localization, captioning and transition-logic understanding.

name: SnapGuard: Lightweight Prompt Injection Detection for Screenshot-Based Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: SnapGuard detects screenshot-based prompt injection through complementary visual-stability and recovered textual cues. Its evaluation compares detection quality and inference cost across attack and benign-page settings.

name: Beyond Screenshots: Evaluating VLMs' Understanding of UI Animations
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AniMINT evaluates how VLMs perceive, explain and interpret UI animations using densely annotated videos. The study distinguishes basic motion recognition from higher-level animation meaning and probes motion, context and perceptual cues.

name: A11y-Compressor: A Framework for Enhancing the Efficiency of GUI Agent Observations through Visual Context Reconstruction and Redundancy Reduction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: A11y-Compressor transforms linearized accessibility trees through modal detection, redundancy reduction and semantic structuring. Its OSWorld evaluation measures both observation-token reduction and task success.

name: AutoFocus: Uncertainty-Aware Active Visual Search for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents AutoFocus, a training-free grounding method that turns sampled coordinates and token uncertainty into spatial region proposals. Shape-aware crops and visual comparison select a target while retaining surrounding interface context.

name: BAMI: Training-Free Bias Mitigation in GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported accuracy change is measured on ScreenSpot-Pro.
summary: BAMI uses coarse-to-fine focus and candidate selection at inference time to address precision and ambiguity errors in GUI grounding.

name: Region4Web: Rethinking Observation Space Granularity for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Reorganizes webpage accessibility trees into functional regions through hierarchical decomposition and semantic abstraction. PageDigest supplies a persistent region-level observation to web agents, evaluated on WebArena.

name: ReVision: Scaling Computer-Use Agents via Temporal Visual Redundancy Reduction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Trains GUI agents with a learned selector that removes repeated visual patches across consecutive screenshots while preserving spatial structure. ReVision evaluates this history representation on OSWorld, WebTailBench and AgentNetBench.

name: What Happens Before Decoding? Prefill Determines GUI Grounding in VLMs
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Re-Prefill adds an attention-guided second prefill pass that revisits candidate screen regions before coordinate generation. The study evaluates this training-free intervention across GUI-grounding models and benchmarks.

name: DRS-GUI: Dynamic Region Search for Training-Free GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: DRS-GUI searches screenshot regions through focus, shift and scatter operations selected by a tree-search planner. A region-quality reward guides this training-free perceptual search before final GUI grounding.

name: ScreenSearch: Uncertainty-Aware OS Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: ScreenSearch explores desktop GUI states by indexing and deduplicating UIA-tree screens, then using outcome ambiguity and frontier rewards to guide graph search.

name: MUIAnno: An Expert-Annotated Dataset and Evaluation Benchmark for Mobile UI Understanding
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MUIAnno provides expert labels for elements in manually explored mobile-app screens, with a web annotation tool that emits structured JSON. It also supplies UI-element detection baselines for the dataset.

name: AQuaUI: Visual Token Reduction for GUI Agents with Adaptive Quadtrees
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: AQuaUI reduces screenshot tokens for GUI agents at inference time with adaptive quadtrees that retain spatial positions and reuse prior tree structure across steps.

name: ChartAct: A Benchmark for Dynamic Chart Understanding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: ChartAct benchmarks multimodal models and GUI agents on interactive charts from websites, requiring actions such as hovering or zooming to answer questions.

name: DiffSpot: Can VLMs Spot Fine-Grained Visual Differences in Web Interfaces?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: DiffSpot benchmarks detection of fine visual changes in rendered web interfaces using image pairs created by single-property CSS mutations.

name: STaR-KV: Spatio-Temporal Adaptive Re-weighting for KV Cache Compression in GUI Vision-Language Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: STaR-KV compresses GUI-agent KV caches by calibrating visual-token importance across attention subspaces and interaction time. Its training-free scoring combines spatial specialization, temporal redundancy and an adaptive temperature, evaluated at matched cache budgets.

name: Context-Aware Workflow Decomposition for Automated Mobile UI Annotation Using Multimodal Large Language Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The experiments use expert-annotated screens from MUIAnno.
summary: Studies staged prompting for automated mobile UI element annotation, comparing workflow depths and element groupings on expert-annotated MUIAnno screens.

name: Benchmarking Living-Screen-Native GUI Agents on Short-Video Platforms
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: LivingScreen evaluates agents in a browser-based short-video environment where observing content consumes time and affects subsequent actions. Its task suite scores accuracy together with information efficiency to diagnose over- and under-observation on continuously changing screens.

name: DragOn: A Benchmark and Dataset for Drag-Based GUI Interactions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: DragOn supplies drag-grounding training data and a held-out benchmark for highlighting text, selecting cells, resizing elements and moving sliders. It evaluates existing vision-language models and a model fine-tuned on the drag tasks.

name: Signal-Driven Observation for Long-Horizon Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract presents an architecture proposal and open problems, without reporting an empirical evaluation.
summary: Proposes Signal-Driven Observation: a separate call selects relevant DOM elements and selectors, and a detector requests new observations only after meaningful browser events or failures. The paper frames observation timing and compression as an architectural research problem for long-horizon web agents.

name: CAPED: Context-Aware Privacy Exposure Defense for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CAPED filters mobile screenshots before upload by combining task requirements, screen context and parsed UI elements to mask incidental private content. AndroidWorld and a controlled seeded privacy evaluation examine leakage reduction alongside task utility and prototype costs.

name: Reasoning for Mobile User Experience with Multimodal LLMs: Task, Benchmark, and Approach
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces UXBench for diagnosing usability issues from UI screenshots and UI-UX, a reinforcement-trained model for reasoning about those interface problems.

name: Running the Gauntlet: Hard Agentic Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v5). The benchmark uses five controlled web-based professional applications.
summary: Introduces GauntletBench, a web-based benchmark of vision-intensive tasks in five professional applications for assessing agent perception, 3D reasoning, and generalisation.

name: VISUALSKILL: Multimodal Skills for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: VISUALSKILL organizes application-specific text and figures into hierarchical skills retrieved on demand through an MCP tool. Skills combine authored documentation with live UI exploration, and matched multimodal/text-only comparisons test their utility for interface identification and workflow-state verification.

name: Agent-Computer Observation Interfaces Enable Dynamic Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: The Agent-Computer Observation Interface separates continuous perception from discrete computer actions using captured frames, audio transcription and persistent visual narration. DynaCU-Bench tests these components on dynamic browser tasks and static controls, with model-specific ablations showing that additional observations can also hurt.

name: GUICrafter: Weakly-Supervised GUI Agent Leveraging Massive Unannotated Screenshots
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: GUICrafter first learns grounding from large collections of unannotated screenshots and webpages, then uses a smaller high-quality dataset for reinforcement-learning calibration. The curriculum targets reduced dependence on manually annotated GUI training data.

name: One Forward Beats Two: InnerZoom for Accurate and Efficient GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: InnerZoom preserves target-region cues from intermediate decoder layers and reinjects a compact evidence state during coordinate decoding. Its single-forward GUI grounder is compared with crop-and-rerun zooming and matched supervised/RL baselines for accuracy and inference cost.

name: LUMOS: A Semantic Operating-System Layer for Accessibility-Grounded AI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: LUMOS converts native accessibility metadata and browser UI structure into semantic interface blueprints with stable element identifiers and available actions. It combines live pointer-to-element grounding with an observe-act loop constrained to visible-UI primitives.

name: Do GUI Agents Believe Their Eyes? Diagnosing State-Belief Reliance on Pixels versus Structure
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Defines visual state reliance and probes whether GUI agents resolve screenshot/structure conflicts using pixels, serialized interface structure or prior beliefs. Paired interventions and live multi-step tests connect misattributed state beliefs to failures and compare consistency-based mitigations.

name: StepX-Edge: An On-Device UI Vision-Language Model via Architecture-Training-Deployment Co-Design
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces StepX-Edge, an on-device UI vision-language model for screen understanding, OCR, question answering, and element grounding on mobile chips.

name: Desktop-Delta Bench: Do Computer-Use Models Understand Desktop GUI Transitions?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Desktop-Delta Bench, an offline diagnostic of GUI transition understanding using temporal-ordering tasks and before/after action inference. It includes decoy observations to test whether models track the source and task relevance of screen changes.

name: GUI-Lens: Coarse-to-Fine Cropping for GUI Grounding with General-Purpose VLMs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: GUI-Lens uses OCR and detected interface components as coordinate references while a general-purpose VLM selects progressively enlarged screenshot crops. Instruction-conditioned checks constrain the crop and click proposals before mapping the final location back to the original screen.

name: Routing Is Least Learnable Where It Is Most Valuable: Bounds on Representation Routing for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Measures the complementarity, cost and rerun variability of six browser observation modes on WebArena and VisualWebArena. Its routing experiments distinguish an oracle cost opportunity from policies that fail to robustly outperform a fixed observation mode.

name: CAP: A Scalable Benchmark for Evaluating Cross-Site Browser Agents with Complex Actions and Perception
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: CAP builds cross-site browser workflows by decomposing websites into operation and perception requirements and recomposing them into tasks. Its judge-based evaluation diagnoses complex interactions and visual-perception failures across real websites.

name: Not an A11y: How Android Accessibility Exposes Mobile AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injection
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Demonstrates that unsanitized Android accessibility tree metadata exposes mobile GUI agents to stealthy indirect prompt injection attacks.

name: Hallucination-Free GUI Grounding via Regression-Free Layout-Aware Matching
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This framework separates frozen-model instruction expansion from a trained layout-aware matcher that localizes GUI elements without coordinate regression. Binary text/icon supervision supports the matcher, with evaluations on GUI grounding and Mind2Web element-selection tasks.

name: ComponentBench: Diagnosing Component-Level Failures in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ComponentBench evaluates short interactions with canonical web UI components using verified tasks and matched human reference trajectories. Its diagnostic pipeline compares observation/action representations and analyzes structural difficulty, failure patterns and interaction efficiency.

name: Lexical Coupling in GUI Element Grounding: Sentence Embeddings Track Labels across Mobile and Web
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies whether text-embedding GUI grounding scores reflect semantic matching or recovery of visible labels. Same-screen ranking comparisons with lexical baselines expose differences between deployable fusion, oracle selection, and performance on label-poor targets.

name: GUI-Primitives: Diagnosing Spatial Reasoning Failures in Vision-Language GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces GUI-Primitives, a paired-instruction benchmark that changes a spatial relation while holding the screenshot and anchor fixed. Its diagnostics separate failure to localize either candidate from failure to choose the candidate satisfying the relation.

name: Reflection with Action-Induced Visual Differences for Desktop GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Evidence-First Reflection, which separates extraction of action-induced screen changes from judgment of whether an operation achieved its objective. It filters visual differences into relevant evidence before a desktop agent’s reflector decides how execution should continue.

name: MCP-Driven Accessibility Tree Standardization for AI-Powered Screen Reader Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Proposes an MCP architecture that presents accessibility trees from Windows, macOS, Android, and web frameworks in a common form for LLM assistive agents interacting with GUIs.

name: Beyond the Verdict: Evidence-Aligned Evaluation of Visual Prompt-Injection Guardrails
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Mind2Web-Injection, a benchmark for evaluating web-agent guardrail decisions on instruction-screenshot pairs using evidence boxes and image-side counterfactuals.

name: TRACE: Trajectory-robust Admission with Evidence Ordering for Efficient GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: TRACE orders screenshot evidence for monotonic visual-token reduction using layout priors, instruction relevance and feature novelty. Spatial token reserves and incremental KV contraction aim to preserve useful evidence for future GUI targets without repeatedly encoding retired frames.

name: LLaDA-UI: Bringing Block-wise Diffusion to Vision-Language GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: LLaDA-UI adapts block-wise diffusion generation to a vision-language GUI agent through multimodal pretraining and GUI supervised fine-tuning. It evaluates grounding and navigation across multiple platform settings.

name: PriMobiBench: Characterizing Visual Privacy Leakage in VLM-Driven Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: PriMobiBench evaluates direct privacy leakage and user profiling from mobile GUI screenshot trajectories, supported by the MobiLeak trace dataset. It also tests masking sensitive, task-irrelevant interface elements before cloud processing and measures the resulting privacy and utility trade-off.

name: When Agents See Differently: Exposing UI Desynchronization Threats in Mobile Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Investigates mismatches between what humans see on a mobile display and what agents receive through screenshots or accessibility metadata. An automated evaluation framework embeds instruction-agnostic perturbations into functional APK clones and compares static and dynamic agent deviations with human noticeability.

name: RankGround: Efficient High-Resolution GUI Grounding via Lightweight Reranker-Guided Crop Selection
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: RankGround trains a lightweight reranker to select a promising screenshot crop before one VLM localization call. Ranking supervision uses containment and boundary-aware augmentation, with pointwise and listwise training stages.

name: Invisible in Space, Visible in Time: Motion Vision CAPTCHA against GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MVCAP-Bench tests live browser CAPTCHAs whose foreground meaning emerges through motion against dynamic backgrounds. A foreground-only control separates temporal camouflage difficulty from answer format and browser interaction.

name: Improving LLM-based Autonomous Web Agents with Filtering
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Trains HTML-element relevance filters on Mind2Web trajectories and transfers them to WebArena to reduce irrelevant browser context. It also evaluates a zero-shot ColBERT retriever and documents baseline web-agent failure modes.

name: OpenVAM: Open-World Visual Attention Modeling with VLMs
notes: Static human-attention modeling on U-EYE webpage screenshots, with FIWI held out from training; no live-browser, agent-action or task-success evaluation. Gemini-generated reference rationales are expert-checked, and JScore compares generated text with references; human validation covers a separate 100-image subset. Reference text and heatmap alignment measure agreement; causal explanations of gaze and temporal scanpaths remain unestablished. Several baseline scores come from prior papers.
summary: Combines dense saliency prediction with explanations of attended elements, including webpage layouts; evaluates human-attention agreement and textual rationales on static inputs.

name: Recurrent Latent Visual Search for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces ReLaViS, which performs recurrent visual search inside a grounding model by repeatedly querying screenshot tokens and feeding the resulting spatial evidence back into the model. Coarse-to-fine supervision is constructed from existing interface-element annotations.

name: PlaySuite: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Interactive Visual Intelligence
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The benchmark uses video games as its interactive setting.
summary: Introduces PlaySuite, a closed-loop video-game benchmark that evaluates interactive visual agents, including computer-use agents, over extended play.

name: When Charts Deceive Web Agents: A Paired Benchmark for Misleading Visualization-Grounded Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces MisVisAgentBench, a paired executable benchmark that changes chart evidence while holding web tasks fixed, to trace how misleading visualizations affect agent decisions and downstream actions.

name: CaptchaAgent: Verifiable Visual Reasoning for CAPTCHA Solving
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Presents CaptchaAgent, which builds an explicit visual representation of objects and relations, refines ambiguous regions, and checks counterfactual consistency before acting on interactive CAPTCHAs.

name: Seg2Click: Learning Pixel-Level Action Masks for GUI Visual Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Recasts GUI grounding as predicting a mask of valid click locations from bounding-box supervision, then derives a click point with a deterministic selection rule.

name: MHVF: Training-Free GUI Grounding via Verification-Guided Multi-Hypothesis Search
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces MHVF, a training-free grounding method that explores several candidate screen regions, verifies them in local views, and uses those checks to guide further search.

name: Towards Safe Autonomy for Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Presents SA-CUA, separating trusted and untrusted visual content using accessibility-derived masking rules and a controlled channel for verifying information before endorsement.

name: STP-GUI: Spatially-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Web-GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces STP-GUI, which selects spatially coherent screenshot windows conditioned on the instruction to reduce visual tokens while retaining useful interface structure.

name: fxBench: Evaluating and Understanding Formula Suggestions in Spreadsheets
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces fxBench, a benchmark of spreadsheet formula suggestions, and examines context selection, intent understanding and formula writing for editing assistance.

name: From Seeing to Reporting: A Theory of Reliable Visual Set Generation in Vision-Language Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GUI grounding is one application of a broader visual reporting method.
summary: FSR models visual reporting and gives inference-time procedures for frozen vision-language models, including screen parsing and GUI target selection.

name: Focused Omni-Modal GUI Agents
notes: Reviewed the complete retained abstract and selected v1 method/evaluation sections. OmniGUI uses episode-disjoint reference-action evaluation with Type Match, Exact Match and Goal Progress; live task-success gains remain unestablished. The Android role is explicit in Appendix D.1.
summary: FocusGUI learns step-specific weights over screenshot, audio, video and interaction-context channels, injecting a compact residual into a frozen decoder without pruning its inputs.

name: PointerBench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Fine-Grained GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: POINTERBENCH is a diagnostic GUI grounding suite covering spreadsheet sub-elements, document characters and targets across professional applications.

name: AgentVQA: A Unified Benchmark for Agentic Visual Understanding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). It evaluates visual understanding offline; web agents are one of five domains.
summary: AgentVQA is an offline visual question-answering benchmark across five agent domains, including web agents and questions involving UI element location.

name: WaitLens: Temporal VLM-Based Adaptive Waiting for Industrial GUI Testing Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its waiting-time evaluation uses recordings from an industrial testing pipeline.
summary: Introduces WaitLens, a vision-language model trained on GUI loading trajectories to decide when testing agents can stop waiting for an interface to load.

name: IGG: A Benchmark for Interactive GUI Grounding under Visibility Constraints
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). IGG uses 16 controllable GUI environments and seven visibility-constraint sub-types.
summary: Introduces Interactive GUI Grounding (IGG), a benchmark that tests whether agents can reveal hidden interface targets through interaction before clicking them.

name: PreView: Enhancing GUI Grounding with Preprocessed Views and Cues
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The grounding models remain frozen, while a lightweight auxiliary model is trained.
summary: Introduces PreView, a screenshot preprocessor that adds cropped views and candidate cues to help existing GUI grounding models identify controls for clicks.

name: Chart the Invisible: Interactive Perception for Hidden-Target Exploration in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported completion results concern tasks that require exploration.
summary: Introduces Hagasu, a scrollable-region perception model that helps GUI agents decide where to swipe to reveal hidden targets, especially on mobile screens.

name: Learning to Look Beyond Screens: Transferable Visual Observation from GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GUI grounding supplies supervision; the study also evaluates transfer beyond interfaces.
summary: Introduces LBS, a vision-language model trained with GUI grounding trajectories and crop-and-inspect decisions to study transfer of active visual observation.

name: UI-UG 2: Advancing Mobile UI Understanding and Generation with Fine-Grained Supervision and Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces UI-UG 2, a mobile UI model trained for component understanding, GUI grounding, and structured interface generation with render-aware RL.

name: MKD2World: A Typed Spatial MarkDown World Model For Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces MKD2World, a desktop web world model that represents interface elements in Typed Spatial Markdown and predicts post-action states, supported by AtomBlock-WebUI annotations.

name: Visual Token Routing: Learning to keep tokens that matter
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract reports evaluation on OSWorld, CUA-World, and video-game action prediction.
summary: Introduces Visual Token Routing (VTR), which selects visual tokens from current and earlier screenshots to reduce computer-use agent inference cost while retaining action-relevant information.

name: LongHorizonUI
notes: Code release of the ICLR 2026 paper "LongHorizonUI: A Unified Framework for Robust long-horizon Task Automation of GUI Agent" (the repository description says ICLR2026; the README cites it with anonymous authors and no link). Each screenshot passes through RapidOCR, the OmniParser v2 YOLO icon detector (downloaded from microsoft/OmniParser-v2.0 on first use) and template matching when an icon template directory is set; the merged elements are drawn as numbered boxes, and that annotated screenshot with a step prompt is what the Gemini, Azure OpenAI or OpenAI model receives. Actions are click, long press, swipe, drag, text input and key press. With the fallback cascade on (the default), an element-index target that fails is retried as a relative point inside the box and then as absolute coordinates with jitter; a progress monitor can roll back to the last committed snapshot, at most three times per task. The README documents only the offline mode, which replays a task's recorded screenshot sequence with either the task description or step-by-step instructions. run.py also has a live subcommand that lists USB-connected devices, but at the reviewed commit AndroidContext never opens a device connection (its context stays None), so device actions return without acting. The repository also has a Gradio app, agents that turn recorded taps and swipes into step descriptions, a scrcpy-based Android recording tool, step-level evaluation scripts and the project page source. The LongGUIBench dataset is not released (the README link is a placeholder), the requirements.txt the README installs from is not in the tree, and the README's Apache-2.0 badge and LICENSE link are not backed by a license file. Not a fork, not archived; no release.
summary: Code for the LongHorizonUI Android agent: OCR plus OmniParser icon detection yields numbered element boxes for an LLM, and failed taps fall back from element index to relative and absolute points with rollback.

name: OpenComet
notes: The README presents it as a Smart India Hackathon entry for problem statement 26171, whose listed organisation is ISRO. The Manifest V3 extension (version 1.31.0 at review) is loaded unpacked in Chrome; the README says Firefox has been built from the same source since v1.17.0. src/content/dom-detector.js paints numbered boxes on interactive elements, and the service worker captures the tab through the Chrome debugger or captureVisibleTab, so screenshots carry those marks. In privacy mode, MediaPipe, YOLO, ViT, Tesseract OCR and regex/checksum PII detectors run in the browser, and src/lib/privacy-firewall.js blocks or blanks a frame when sanitizing fails. Actions use selectors, with debugger Input.dispatchMouseEvent clicks where needed, inside a tab-group sandbox with an approval mode. Models: on-device Gemma 4, cloud providers, or Ollama through the bundled server. OpenCometBench is the repository's own test suite; its PII precision/recall uses a synthetic corpus built from the detector's own rules, as the README states, leaving independence outside the measurement.

notes: Distributed through npm (npx native-devtools-mcp; version 0.10.1 in npm/package.json and Cargo.toml at the inspected commit) and as a signed macOS app for Claude Desktop.
